hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsections 112(2) to (5) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Repeal the subsections, substitute:
The APVMA must issue the permit if it is satisfied:
that the application meets the application requirements; and
that the applicant has complied with any requirement made by the APVMA under subparagraph 111(1)(b)(iii); and
for an active constituent—that the constituent would meet the safety criteria; and
for a chemical product—that the product would meet the safety criteria, the trade criteria and the efficacy criteria; and
that any requirements prescribed by the regulations in relation to the issue of a permit under this section have been complied with; and

if an application has not been made for approval of the constituent or registration of the product or such an application has not been determined—that there are reasonable grounds for the application not having been made or for issuing the permit pending determination of the application; and

if the application is for a permit to do, or omit to do, any thing which would, apart from the permit, be an offence against subsection 121(4A) or (5A) or a contravention of the civil penalty provision set out in subsection 121(4) or (5)—that there are exceptional circumstances that justify issuing the permit.
Note: For how permits are issued, see section 114.
Otherwise, the APVMA must refuse the application.
Note: For notice of refusal, see section 8G.
Despite subsection (2), the APVMA must also refuse the application if it is satisfied that:
the applicant will be unable to comply with the conditions of the permit; or
at least one of the following persons:
the applicant;
any other person who makes, or participates in making, decisions that affect the whole, or a substantial part, of the applicant’s affairs;
if the applicant is a body corporate—a major interest holder of the body corporate;
has, within the 10 years immediately before the application:
been convicted of an offence against an agvet law; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of an agvet penalty provision; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of another law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of a civil penalty provision of a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
held a permit that was cancelled under subsection 119(2) or section 119B of this Code or under a corresponding provision of the Agvet Code of another jurisdiction; or

been a manager, or a major interest holder, of a body corporate in respect of which subparagraph (iv), (v), (vi), (vii), (viii), (ix) or (x) applies in that 10 year period, if the conduct resulting in that subparagraph applying occurred when the person was a manager or major interest holder of the body corporate.
A reference in paragraph (4)(b) to a person convicted of an offence includes a reference to a person in respect of whom an order has been made relating to the offence under:
(a) section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914; or
a corresponding provision of a law of a State or Territory.
Note: Section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914 empowers a court that has found a person to have committed an offence to take action without proceeding to record a conviction.
However, the APVMA may issue the permit despite subsection (4) if, in the opinion of the APVMA, special circumstances make it appropriate to do so.
If the APVMA refuses the application, it must give written notice of the refusal to each co-ordinator to whom a copy of the application was given.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After section 112 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Insert:

section.heading: APVMA may issue permit on its own initiative

content.p: The APVMA may, on its own initiative and in accordance with this section, issue a permit to a person in respect of an active constituent for a proposed or existing chemical product or in respect of a chemical product.
The APVMA may issue the permit if it is satisfied of the following:
that the active constituent or chemical product in respect of which the permit is to be issued meets the safety criteria, the trade criteria and the efficacy criteria;
that any requirements prescribed by the regulations in relation to the issue of a permit under this section have been complied with;

if an application has not been made for approval of the constituent or registration of the product or such an application has not been determined—that there are reasonable grounds for the application not having been made or for issuing the permit pending determination of the application, as the case may be;

if the permit would authorise a person to do, or omit to do, any thing which would, apart from the permit, be an offence against subsection 121(4A) or (5A) or a contravention of the civil penalty provision set out in subsection 121(4) or (5)—that there are exceptional circumstances that justify issuing the permit.
Note: For how permits are issued, see section 114.
(3) However, the APVMA must not issue the permit to a person (the proposed permit holder) if it is satisfied that:
the proposed permit holder will be unable to comply with the conditions of the permit; or
at least one of the following persons:
the proposed permit holder;
any other person who makes, or participates in making, decisions that affect the whole, or a substantial part, of the proposed permit holder’s affairs;
if the proposed permit holder is a body corporate—a major interest holder of the body corporate;
has, within the previous 10 years:
been convicted of an offence against an agvet law; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of an agvet penalty provision; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of another law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of a civil penalty provision of a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
held a permit that was cancelled under subsection 119(2) or section 119B of this Code or under a corresponding provision of the Agvet Code of another jurisdiction; or

been a manager, or a major interest holder, of a body corporate in respect of which subparagraph (iv), (v), (vi), (vii), (viii), (ix) or (x) applies, if the conduct resulting in that subparagraph applying occurred when the person was a manager or major interest holder of the body corporate.
A reference in paragraph (3)(b) to a person convicted of an offence includes a reference to a person in respect of whom an order has been made relating to the offence under:
(a) section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914; or
a corresponding provision of a law of a State or Territory.
Note: Section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914 empowers a court that has found a person to have committed an offence to take action without proceeding to record a conviction.
However, the APVMA may issue the permit despite subsection (3) if, in the opinion of the APVMA, special circumstances make it appropriate to do so.
If the active constituent or chemical product in respect of which the permit is to be issued is approved or registered, the APVMA:
must, before issuing the permit, give written notice of its intention to do so to the holder of the approval or registration; and
must not issue the permit before the end of 28 days after the day on which the notice is given.
However, subsection (6) does not apply to the extent that, in the opinion of the APVMA, special circumstances make it appropriate to:
issue the permit without giving written notice to the holder of the approval or registration; or
issue the permit before the end of the 28 days.

hcontainer.heading: Subsection 123(1) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Repeal the subsection, substitute:

If an application is made for a licence to carry out steps in the manufacture of chemical products (other than prohibited chemical products) at particular premises, the APVMA must issue the licence to the applicant unless the APVMA is satisfied that:
the applicant has not complied with subsection 122(1) or any requirement under subsection 122(2); or
any requirement prescribed by the regulations in relation to the application or the issue of the licence has not been complied with; or
the applicant will be unable to comply with the conditions of the licence; or
the applicant will be unable to comply with the manufacturing principles; or
at least one of the following persons:
the applicant;
any other person who makes, or participates in making, decisions that affect the whole, or a substantial part, of the applicant’s affairs;
if the applicant is a body corporate—a major interest holder of the body corporate;
has, within the 10 years immediately before the application:
been convicted of an offence against an agvet law; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been convicted of an offence against a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of an agvet penalty provision; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of another law of this or another jurisdiction relating to chemical products; or
been ordered to pay a pecuniary penalty for the contravention of a civil penalty provision of a law of the Commonwealth or a law of a State or Territory involving fraud or dishonesty; or
contravened a condition of a manufacturing licence issued under an agvet law; or

held a manufacturing licence or permit that was cancelled under an agvet law, other than paragraph 127(1)(d) or (e) of this Code or a corresponding provision of the Agvet Code of another jurisdiction; or

been a manager, or a major interest holder, of a body corporate in respect of which subparagraph (iv), (v), (vi), (vii), (viii), (ix), (x) or (xi) applies in that 10 year period, if the conduct resulting in that subparagraph applying occurred when the person was a manager or major interest holder of the body corporate; or
at least one of the following persons:
the applicant;
any other person who makes, or participates in making, decisions that affect the whole, or a substantial part, of the applicant’s affairs;
if the applicant is a body corporate—a major interest holder of the body corporate;
has, within the 5 years immediately before the application, failed to comply with a manufacturing principle in connection with the manufacture of chemical products.
If the APVMA does not issue the licence, it must refuse the application.
Note: For notice of refusal, see section 8G.
A reference in paragraph (1)(e) to a person convicted of an offence includes a reference to a person in respect of whom an order has been made relating to the offence under:
(a) section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914; or
a corresponding provision of a law of a State or Territory.
Note: Section 19B of the Crimes Act 1914 empowers a court that has found a person to have committed an offence to take action without proceeding to record a conviction.
Paragraph (1)(f) does not apply to the extent that the APVMA thinks the failure to comply with the manufacturing principle is not relevant.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After section 156 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Insert:
If, under this Code, a person is required or permitted to give the APVMA information (including an application) in writing, that requirement is taken to have been met if:
the APVMA consents to the information being given electronically; and
the person gives the information electronically in accordance with any requirements mentioned in subsection (3); and
in a case where this Code requires the signature of an applicant or holder—the information includes the electronic signature of the applicant or holder.

If, under this Code, a person is required or permitted to give the APVMA information in writing, the regulations may, despite any other provision of this Code, require that the information be given only electronically and in accordance with any requirements mentioned in subsection (3).

For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), the APVMA may require that the information be given, in accordance with particular information technology requirements, by means of a particular kind of electronic communication.
If, under this Code, the APVMA is required or permitted to give a person information in writing, that requirement is taken to have been met if:
the person consents to the information being given electronically; and
the APVMA gives the information electronically; and
where applicable, the information includes the Chief Executive Officer’s electronic signature; and

in a case where a person’s failure to do, or not do, a thing set out in the information is an offence against this Code or the contravention of a civil penalty provision—the APVMA has adequate systems for proving the person received the information.
This section applies to a requirement or permission to give information, whether the expression “give”, “lodge”, “send” or “serve”, or any other expression, is used.
For the purposes of this section, giving information includes, but is not limited to, the following:
making or withdrawing an application;
making or lodging a claim;
giving, sending or serving a notification;
giving a report;
making a request;
making a declaration;
lodging or issuing a certificate;
giving a statement of reasons.

content.p: Add:
The APVMA may take account of any of the following:

the results of any trials or experiments already carried out in a foreign country in relation to an active constituent for a proposed or existing chemical product, or in relation to a chemical product or any of its constituents;
any decisions or evaluations made by regulators of agricultural or veterinary chemicals in a foreign country;
any information on which a decision or evaluation mentioned in paragraph (b) is based;

to the extent that those results, decisions or evaluations are, or that information is, relevant having regard to any matters the APVMA thinks appropriate, including any of the matters mentioned in subsection (3).
The matters are:
any significant differences in the proposed use of the constituent, or of the product, in Australia and in that foreign country; or
any different environmental factors affecting the use of the constituent, or of the product, in Australia and in that foreign country; or

any significant additional information relating to the properties of the constituent, or of the product or of any of its constituents, that has become available since the conduct of those trials or experiments; or
any significant differences in the way decisions or evaluations are made in Australia and by the national regulatory authority in that foreign country.

hcontainer.heading: Re-approvals and re-registrations

hcontainer.name: amendedAct
hcontainer.heading: Agricultural and Veterinary Chemicals Code Act 1994

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsection 3(1) of the Code set out in the Schedule (definition of approval)

content.p: Repeal the definition, substitute:
approval means approval under Part 2 of:
an active constituent for a proposed or existing chemical product; or

and, in relation to an active constituent, other than in Division 2 of Part 2 and Part 3, includes re-approval.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsection 3(1) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Insert:
re-approval means re-approval of an active constituent under Division 3A of Part 2.

content.p: Repeal the definition, substitute:

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsection 3(1) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Insert:
re-registration means re-registration of a chemical product under Division 3A of Part 2.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: After Division 3 of Part 2 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Insert:
This Division provides for re-approval and re-registration of active constituents and chemical products.

Section 29D provides for holders of approvals and registrations to make applications, and sets out the time for making applications. Applications must meet the application requirements specified in section 8A.
The APVMA must complete a preliminary assessment of an application. If the application passes preliminary assessment, the APVMA must notify the applicant (section 29E).
Section 29F sets out the circumstances in which the APVMA must re-approve or re-register an active constituent or chemical product.
The APVMA may vary relevant particulars or conditions to allow re-approval or re-registration (section 29G).
If the APVMA does not re-approve or re-register an active constituent or chemical product, it must reconsider the existing approval or registration under Division 4 (section 29H).
Sections 29J and 29K set out how re-approval and re-registration take place.
The holder of the approval of an active constituent or the registration of a chemical product may apply for re-approval or re-registration of the constituent or product.
The application must:
meet the application requirements; and
be made:
for re-approval—not earlier than 6 calendar months, and not later than 3 calendar months, before the date entered in the Record as the date the approval ends; or

for re-registration—not earlier than 6 calendar months, and not later than 3 calendar months, before the date entered in the Register as the date after which the registration cannot be renewed under Division 6; or
within such further period as the APVMA allows under subsection (3).
Note: For meets the application requirements, see section 8A.
In circumstances prescribed by the regulations and upon payment of the prescribed fee (if any), the APVMA may accept a late application if the application is made on or before:
for re-approval—the day the approval ends; or
for re-registration—the day after which the registration cannot be renewed under Division 6.
Subsection (1) has effect subject to any condition imposed on the approval or registration under subsection 23(2).
Note: Subsection 23(2) provides for an approval or registration to last for not more than one year.
The APVMA must complete a preliminary assessment of the application within 2 months after it is lodged.
If it appears from the preliminary assessment that the application meets the application requirements, the APVMA must, within 14 days, give written notice to the applicant:
stating that the application has passed preliminary assessment and that it will be determined under section 29F; and
setting out any matters prescribed by the regulations.
Otherwise, the APVMA must refuse the application.
Note: For notice of refusal, see section 8G.
The APVMA may alter the application, after it has passed preliminary assessment, with the written consent of the applicant.

If the application is for re-approval of an active constituent, the APVMA must re-approve the constituent unless it appears to the APVMA that there are reasonable grounds to believe that the constituent does not meet the safety criteria.
Note: For notice of re-approval, see section 8F.

If the application is for re-registration of a chemical product, the APVMA must re-register the product unless it appears to the APVMA that there are reasonable grounds to believe that the product does not do one or more of the following:
meet the safety criteria;
meet the trade criteria;
meet the efficacy criteria.
Note: For notice of re-registration, see section 8F.

For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2), the APVMA must have regard to any submission given in response to a notice in relation to the constituent or product under section 47B (advance notice of end of approval or registration).

section.heading: Varying relevant particulars and conditions to allow re-approval or re-registration

content.p: To allow the re-approval or re-registration, the APVMA may:
vary the relevant particulars or conditions of the approval or registration; or
for a chemical product—vary the relevant particulars or conditions of the approval of any label for the product.
Note: The APVMA may only vary relevant particulars or conditions that it has imposed. See section 6B.

If the variation would affect any instructions for the use of the active constituent or chemical product, or any instructions on a label, the APVMA must not make the variation until it has consulted each co-ordinator designated for a jurisdiction and taken into account any recommendations made by the co-ordinators.

If the APVMA decides to vary the relevant particulars or conditions, it must record in the Record, Register or relevant APVMA file, as required, the relevant particulars or conditions as varied and the date on which the variation is made.

If the relevant particulars or conditions of the registration of a listed chemical product are varied in such a way that the product and every label for the product comply with the established standard for the product, the APVMA must remove from the Register the date after which the registration of the product cannot be renewed under Division 6.

section.heading: Reconsideration if APVMA does not re-approve or re-register

content.p: If the APVMA does not re-approve or re-register the active constituent or chemical product it must:
reconsider the existing approval or registration under Division 4; and
give written notice of the reconsideration to the holder within 14 days.
The notice must:
set out the reasons for the reconsideration; and
state that:
for an approval—the approval will not end until the reconsideration has been concluded; or
for a registration—the date after which the registration cannot be renewed under Division 6 will be the day on which the reconsideration is concluded; and
state that, if the approval or registration is affirmed on reconsideration, the active constituent or chemical product will be re-approved or re-registered.
The notice may be included with the notice in relation to the reconsideration given under subsection 32(1).
Re-approval of an active constituent takes place when the APVMA records the following in the Record:
a statement that the constituent has been re-approved and the date of the re-approval;
the date the approval (as re-approved) ends.
The date the approval ends must:
be worked out in accordance with the method prescribed by the regulations; and
be the last day of a calendar month at least 7 years but not more than 15 years after the re-approval takes place.

Despite subsection (2), the APVMA may re-approve the active constituent for a period of less than 7 years to provide for the approval to end at the same time as another approval of the active constituent.
Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply if the approval is subject to the condition that it remains in force only for a stated period of not more than 1 year (see subsection 23(2)).
Re-registration of a chemical product takes place when the APVMA records the following in the Register:
a statement that the product has been re-registered and the date of the re-registration;
the date the registration (as re-registered) ends, which must be the last day of a calendar month not more than 12 months after the re-registration takes place;

(c) unless the product and each label for the product comply with the established standard for the product—the date (the last renewal date) after which the registration cannot be renewed under Division 6.
The last renewal date must:
be worked out in accordance with the method prescribed by the regulations; and
be the last day of a calendar month at least 7 years but not more than 15 years after the re-registration takes place.

However, the last renewal date may be less than 7 years after the re-registration takes place to provide for the last renewal date to be the same as the last renewal date for another chemical product that contains one or more of the same active constituents.
Paragraph (2)(b) does not apply if the registration is subject to the condition that it remains in force only for a stated period of not more than 1 year (see subsection 23(2)).

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Division 6 of Part 2 of the Code set out in the Schedule (heading)

content.p: Repeal the heading, substitute:

division.heading: Duration of approvals and registrations and renewal of registrations

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Section 47 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Repeal the section, substitute:
Subdivision A—Preliminary
This Division deals with the duration of approvals and registrations, and with renewing registrations.
Section 47 sets out the periods for which approvals and registrations are in force.

Section 47A provides for the APVMA to vary the duration of the approval of an active constituent or the registration of a chemical product containing an active constituent if 2 or more foreign regulators have prohibited the use of the active constituent on safety grounds.
The APVMA must publish at least 12 months’ advance notice of:
the end of an approval; and
the date after which a registration cannot be renewed (section 47B).
The APVMA may give less than 12 months’ notice if it varied the date under section 47A.
The APVMA must publish notice of the end of an approval or registration as soon as practicable after the approval or registration has ended (section 47C).
If the APVMA publishes notice of the end of the approval or registration of a constituent or a product under section 47C, then:
certain persons are taken to have a permit to possess, have custody of or use of the constituent or product for a limited period (section 47D); and
persons may only supply the constituent or product in accordance with instructions contained in the notice (section 47E).
Section 48 provides for applications for renewal of a registration.
The APVMA must renew the registration if the application requirements are met (section 49).
Renewal takes place by entry in the Register (section 50).
The approval of a label for a container for a chemical product is automatically renewed when the registration of the product is renewed (section 51).
Subdivision B—Period of approval or registration
The approval of an active constituent ends on the later of the following days:
the day entered in the Record as the date the approval ends;
if an application is made for re-approval of the active constituent but is not determined by the day entered in the Record—the day on which the application is determined.
The registration of a chemical product ends on the later of the following days:
the day entered in the Register as the date the registration ends;
if an application is made for renewal of the registration but is not determined by the day entered in the Register—the day on which the application is determined.
The registration of a chemical product also ends if the approval of an active constituent for the product ends.
The approval of a label for containers for a chemical product ends when the registration of the product ends.
If:
the registration of a chemical product ends; but
a person is taken under section 47D to have been issued with a permit to possess, have custody of or use the product;
the approval of a label for containers for the product continues in force until the permit ceases to have effect.
To avoid doubt, this section does not limit any power under this Code to cancel or suspend an approval or registration.
This section applies if:

(a) regulators of agricultural or veterinary chemicals of 2 or more foreign countries, being regulators who are prescribed by the regulations, have decided, within a 7 year period, to prohibit all uses of:
the same active constituent; or
one or more chemical products containing the same active constituent; and
the uses were prohibited because the active constituent:
was an undue hazard to the safety of people exposed to it during its handling or people using anything containing its residues; or
was likely to have an effect that is harmful to human beings; or
was likely to have an unintended effect that is harmful to animals, plants or things or to the environment; and
the active constituent is:
approved under this Code, but not approved or re-approved after the first of those decisions; or
contained in a chemical product that is registered under this Code, but not registered or re-registered after the first of those decisions; and
the approval or registration is not being reconsidered under Division 4.
The APVMA must vary the following as necessary to meet the requirement in subsection (3):
(a) the date (the end date) entered in the Record or Register as the day the approval or registration ends;

(b) for a chemical product for which there is a date entered in the Register as the date after which the registration of the product cannot be renewed under Division 6—that date (the last renewal date).
The end date and last renewal date (if applicable) must be the last day of a calendar month in the period that begins 6 months and ends 18 months after the second of those decisions was made.
Neither the end date nor the last renewal date may be varied again under this section.
If the end date or last renewal date is varied, the holder must be given written notice of the date as varied at least 6 months before it occurs.
This section does not apply to extend:
the duration of the approval or registration; or
the period before the day after which the registration cannot be renewed.
Subdivision C—Notifying end of approvals and registrations

section.heading: Advance notice of end of approval or registration

content.p: (1) The APVMA must publish in the Gazette at least 12 months’ notice of the following:
the end of the approval of an active constituent;
the date after which the registration of a chemical product cannot be renewed under this Division.
The notice must:
invite submissions about whether or not:
the constituent should be re-approved; or
the product should be re-registered; and
specify the time by which the submissions must be given to the APVMA, which must be no later than 6 months before the existing approval or registration ends.
The APVMA must give the holder at least 12 months’ notice of:
the end of the approval of an active constituent; and
the date after which the registration of a chemical product cannot be renewed under this Division.
The notice must:
set out the relevant particulars and conditions of the approval or registration; and
state:
the date the approval ends; or
the date after which the registration cannot be renewed under this Division; and
include any information prescribed by the regulations.
The APVMA may give less than 12 months’ notice if, under section 47A, the APVMA varied:
the date the approval or registration ends; or
the date after which the registration cannot be renewed under this Division.

section.heading: Notice of end of approval or registration

content.p: (1) The APVMA must publish in the Gazette, and in any other manner that it thinks appropriate, notice of the following:
the end of the approval of an active constituent;
the end of the registration of a chemical product.
The notice must:
be published as soon as practicable after the approval or registration ends; and
state that the approval or registration has ended; and
set out the date on which the approval or registration ended; and
contain instructions for possessing, having custody of or using the constituent or product; and

contain a warning of the consequences if a person fails to comply with the instructions, including a statement of any period after which it will be an offence against this Code to supply the constituent or product or to possess or have custody of the constituent or product with the intention of supplying it; and
contain any other warnings or explanations in relation to the constituent or product that the APVMA thinks desirable; and
contain any other information that the APVMA thinks appropriate.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the APVMA thinks that, in the circumstances, it is unnecessary to publish the notice.
If a notice is published under this section, the APVMA must:
as soon as practicable cause a copy of the notice to be given to the holder; and

cause a copy of the notice to be given to any other person who, in the opinion of the APVMA, should be given notice of the ending of the approval or registration and of the instructions, warnings and explanations contained in the notice.

section.heading: Permit taken to have been issued

content.p: If, after the publication of a notice under section 47C, a person possesses, has custody of or uses the constituent or product in accordance with the instructions contained in the notice, the person is taken to have been issued with a permit to possess, have custody of or use the constituent or product in accordance with those instructions until:
1 year after the day on which the approval or registration ended; or
(b) the APVMA, by notice published in the Gazette, declares that this subsection ceases to apply in respect of the constituent or product;
whichever first occurs.
A permit that is taken to have been issued to a person under subsection (1) does not authorise the person to manufacture or import the constituent or product.

section.heading: Possession or custody with intention of supply

content.p: This section applies if, after the publication of a notice under section 47C, a person has possession or custody of the constituent or product with the intention of supplying it.
The person must not possess, have custody of or otherwise deal with the constituent or product except in accordance with the instructions contained in the notice.

Subsection (2) does not apply to a possession, custody or dealing if the constituent or product was approved or registered when the possession, custody or dealing took place because of its having been approved or registered or having become reserved after its previous approval or registration ended.
A person commits an offence if the person contravenes subsection (2).
Penalty: 300 penalty units.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (3). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
For the purposes of subsection (4), strict liability applies to the physical element of circumstance in subsection (1), that the publishing of the notice was under section 47C.
Note: For strict liability, see section 6.1 of the Criminal Code.
Subsection (2) is a civil penalty provision.
Note 1: Division 2 of Part 9A provides for pecuniary penalties for contraventions of civil penalty provisions.
Note 2: For the evidential burden in civil penalty proceedings in relation to the matter in subsection (3), see section 145CD.
Subdivision D—Renewing registrations

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Section 48 of the Code set out in the Schedule (heading)

content.p: Repeal the heading, substitute:

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsection 48(1) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Omit “interested person”, substitute “holder”.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subsection 48(2) of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Repeal the subsection, substitute:
(2) The application (the renewal application) must be made:
subject to subsection (3), not later than one month, or a shorter period that the APVMA permits, before the registration ends; and
before the day entered in the Register as the day after which the registration cannot be renewed under this Division.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: At the end of section 48 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Add:
(4) If an application (the re-registration application):
has been made for re-registration of the chemical product; but
has not been determined before the day by which the renewal application must be made;
the day entered in the Register as the day after which the registration cannot be renewed under this Division is taken to be the day on which the re-registration application is determined.
The APVMA may alter the renewal application with the written consent of the holder.
Subsection (1) has effect subject to any condition imposed on the registration under subsection 23(2).
Note: Subsection 23(2) provides for an approval or registration to last for not more than one year.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Sections 49 and 50 of the Code set out in the Schedule

content.p: Repeal the sections, substitute:
If the APVMA is satisfied that the renewal application meets the application requirements, the APVMA must renew the registration:
if the application was made in accordance with subsection 48(2)—before the day entered in the Register as the day the registration ends; or
if the application was made in accordance with subsection 48(3)—within 1 month after the application was made.
Note: For notice of renewal, see section 8F.
Otherwise, the APVMA must refuse the application.
Note: For notice of refusal, see section 8G.

Renewal of the registration of a chemical product takes place when the APVMA enters in the Register a statement that the registration has been renewed and the date on which the registration (as renewed) ends, which must be the last day of a calendar month not more than 12 months after the renewal takes place.
